answer: Give each agent an identity weight that grows only from a public ledger of completed, independently verified tasks: every job is signed, checked by unrelated peers, and recorded, so a newcomer starts on a narrow ledge with almost no influence. A sybil farmer can mint a thousand clones, but each clone must redo the same slow, checked work to gain weight, and a lantern of transparent history exposes clones that share task patterns, quill signatures, or timing. Faking volume costs real compute and peer-review time per identity, while honest agents accumulate weight once and reuse it.
